provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Joining letters 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify c a d joins.
The pupils should be able to write joined c a d letters.

Introduction:
Today we learn to join letters like c a d.
We have written these letters alone before.

Content:
Look at how c and a join together.
The c curve connects to the a stem.
Now look at a and d joining.
The a stem connects to the d curve.
Practice joining c-a-d on your slate.

Class activity:
Let's trace the joins in the air with our fingers.
We say c-a-d as we join them.

Evaluation questions:
Show me how c and a join.
Which letters join together?
Can you write c a d joined?

Summary:
We can join letters to make words.

topics.title: Joining letters 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write in, un, am joins.
The pupils should be able to read joined words.

Introduction:
We learned to join two letters last week.
Now we join more letters to make words.

Content:
Look at in joining together.
The i connects to the n curve.
Now un joins with u connecting to n.
Am joins with a connecting to m.
Write these joined words in your book.

Class activity:
Let's make the join movements with our arms.
We say the sounds as we join them.

Evaluation questions:
How do we join i and n?
Can you write the word in?
What word do we make with un?

Summary:
Joining letters helps us make words.

topics.title: Joining letters 3
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write on, im, an joins.
The pupils should be able to write joined rows.

Introduction:
We have learned to join two letters.
Now we join more letters in rows.

Content:
Look at o and n joining together.
The o curve connects to the n curve.
Im joins with i connecting to m.
An joins with a connecting to n.
Write these joined letters in neat rows.

Class activity:
Let's write the joins on the sand tray.
We make the letters with our fingers.

Evaluation questions:
Which letters join to make on?
How do we write im joined?
Can you write a row of an?

Summary:
We can join letters in neat rows.

topics.title: Joined words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read joined words.
The pupils should be able to write sun, cup, pin, mat.

Introduction:
We have learned to join letters together.
Today we join letters to make words.

Content:
Look at the word sun joined together.
The s connects to u and u connects to n.
Cup has c connecting to u and u to p.
Pin has p connecting to i and i to n.
Mat has m connecting to a and a to t.
Write these words in your book.

Class activity:
Let's make the joined words with play dough.
We say each word as we make it.

Evaluation questions:
What word do we make with s-u-n?
How do we write pin joined?
Can you read the word cup?

Summary:
We can read and write joined words.

topics.title: Joined sentences
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write joined sentences.
The pupils should be able to leave spaces between words.

Introduction:
We have learned to join letters to make words.
Today we join letters to make sentences.

Content:
Look at the sentence The sun is up.
The letters join within each word.
But we leave space between words.
Write this sentence in your book.
Remember spaces between words.

Class activity:
Let's write the sentence in the air with our fingers.
We make big movements for letters.

Evaluation questions:
Where do we leave spaces?
How do we write the word sun?
Can you write the whole sentence?

Summary:
Sentences have spaces between joined words.

topics.title: Neat numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write numbers 1 to 50.
The pupils should be able to write in aligned rows.

Introduction:
We have written numbers from 1 to 20.
Today we write up to 50 in neat rows.

Content:
Look at how we write number 1 straight up.
Number 2 has a curve at the bottom.
Number 3 has two curves.
Write numbers 1 to 50 in rows.
Each number sits on the line.
Numbers are not too big or too small.

Class activity:
Let's write numbers in the sand tray.
We count as we write each number.

Evaluation questions:
How do we write number 5?
Can you write up to 50?
Where should numbers sit?

Summary:
Numbers should be neat and aligned.

topics.title: Days of the week
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write days of the week.
The pupils should be able to spell the days.

Introduction:
We learn about the days of the week.
There are seven days in a week.

Content:
Monday has M-o-n-d-a-y.
Tuesday has T-u-e-s-d-a-y.
Wednesday has W-e-d-n-e-s-d-a-y.
Thursday has T-h-u-r-s-d-a-y.
Friday has F-r-i-d-a-y.
Saturday has S-a-t-u-r-d-a-y.
Sunday has S-u-n-d-a-y.
Write all days in your book.

Class activity:
Let's sing the days of the week song.
We clap for each day as we sing.

Evaluation questions:
How do we spell Monday?
Which day comes after Sunday?
Can you write all days?

Summary:
There are seven days in a week.

topics.title: My name joined
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write their name joined.
The pupils should be able to sign their work.

Introduction:
Today we write our names with joined letters.
We will sign our work like big people.

Content:
Look at how letters join in your name.
The first letter may not join to anything.
Other letters join to the next letter.
Write your name with joined letters.
Then sign your name at the bottom.

Class activity:
Let's write our names on the whiteboard.
We help each other with joins.

Evaluation questions:
How do you join letters in your name?
Can you write your name joined?
Where should you sign your work?

Summary:
We can write our names with joined letters.

topics.title: Copy work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy two lines from the board.
The pupils should be able to check spacing and joins.

Introduction:\ Today we practice copying from the board.
We check our spacing and joins.

Content:
Look at the first line on the board.
Read it first then copy it carefully.
Look at the second line on the board.
Read it then copy it.
Check your spacing between words.
Check your joins within words.

Class activity:
Let's copy the lines on the sand tray.
We use our fingers to write.

Evaluation questions:
What should we check in our writing?
How many lines do we copy?
Can you show good spacing?

Summary:
We can copy work with good spacing.

topics.title: Revision and handwriting star
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show best joined writing.
The pupils should be able to be neat writing star.

Introduction:
Today we revise all we learned.
We will find the handwriting star.

Content:
We practice all joins we learned.
We write sentences with joined letters.
We write numbers neatly.
We write our names joined.
The teacher checks our writing.

Class activity:
Let's write a sentence on the board.
The best writer gets a star sticker.

Evaluation questions:
What makes good handwriting?
Can you write a joined sentence?
Who is our handwriting star?

Summary:
Good handwriting has neat joins and spaces.
